bullets.markup: Co-designed a transfer planner: a **FastAPI** backend that matches courses to official ASSIST agreements with deterministic rules (minimum grades, agreement years), a **React** and **TypeScript** interface, and **Supabase**.

**Claude** reads transcripts and class schedules that students confirm and answers with numbered citations that code validates; **Apify** scrapes campus pages and a **Factory Droid** agent repairs only broken scraper scripts, in a sandbox.
Kept data grounded: **Apify** scrapes campus pages, a **Factory Droid** agent repairs broken scrapers under deny-by-default permissions, and guide items must quote their source.
**Claude** reads confirmed transcripts and answers with sources; **Apify** scrapes campus pages, a **Factory Droid** agent repairs broken scrapers, and **Supabase** stores student data.
Tested with **10** transfer students, who said it would have helped during their own transfer.
Built with **Claude**: a **Python** and **FastAPI** app that tailors a **LaTeX** resume to a job posting.
**Claude API** rewrites must quote my own records; code rejects invented numbers and checks page fit and ATS parsing.
Built a tool that tailors a one-page LaTeX resume to a job posting, leaving the layout untouched and rewriting only the bullet text.
Rejects any rewrite that lacks a quote from my own records, and checks that the PDF fits one page and passes ATS parsing.
Built a multi-label NLP model that predicts a movie's genres from its title, tagline, and plot, using MiniLM, MPNet, and e5-large-v2 text embeddings on **42K+** films.

Compared Logistic Regression, XGBoost, and LightGBM: Logistic Regression won and trained about **12×** faster than XGBoost; dropping rare genres and tuning the threshold raised Macro F1 from 0.48 to **0.66**.
Embedded each film's text with MiniLM, MPNet, and e5-large-v2 and found the largest model (e5-large-v2) gave the best genre predictions.
Compared Logistic Regression, XGBoost, and LightGBM on text embeddings; the simpler Logistic Regression won and trained about **12×** faster.

Built a model that estimates home values from **200K+** Cook County (Chicago) property records, and audited its fairness across price ranges to show which homes get over- or under-valued and taxed unfairly.
Built a model that estimates home values from **200K+** Chicago-area property records and checked which homes are over- or under-valued.
Engineered **15+** features (log square footage, polynomial age and location terms) and validated with 4-fold cross-validation (test RMSE **0.562**).

Mapped the parts of Los Angeles that qualify for denser housing near transit under a new California law (**6,413** eligible zoning areas), layering in displacement risk, pollution, and fire hazard data in an interactive StoryMap.
Built a spam filter that reads an email's text and flags spam, correctly sorting **92.1%** of emails it had never seen.
Built a spam filter from 50+ engineered signals (link counts, dollar signs, HTML) that correctly sorts **92.1%** of unseen emails.
Tuned an L1-regularized Logistic Regression with GridSearchCV and **10**-fold cross-validation, weighing precision against recall because false positives cost more.
Building the ML pipeline for a smart-glasses app that turns a day of footage into a **60-second** recap.
Building **CLIP ViT-B/32** clip embeddings in PyTorch and OpenCV, checked with cosine-similarity neighbors.
ML team member on a smart-glasses recap app, embedding clips with CLIP to rank them for the **60**-second video.

Building the ML pipeline for an app that turns a day of Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses footage into a **60-second** highlight video, splitting footage into clips and using audio and visual models to pick the best moments.
Work with the iOS and backend teams on how clip ranking fits into the full product pipeline.

Writing the clip embedding stage in Python: samples evenly spaced frames per clip with OpenCV, encodes them with a pretrained **CLIP ViT-B/32** model in PyTorch, then averages and L2-normalizes them into one vector per clip.
Built a seeded, procedurally generated dungeon game in Java where enemies chase the player along shortest paths (BFS), moving two steps for every one the player takes once in range.
Designed a quiz-battle system with **100+** CS 61B trivia questions: enemy contact drains health until the player answers correctly, and health packs restore it.
Built a word-exploration tool that finds every more specific word under a given word and ranks them by usage.
Implemented hyponym search over a WordNet graph with recursive DFS, and wrote tests for cycles, self-loops, and disconnected graphs.
Built a Python program that runs Scheme code, with tail-call optimization so deep recursion does not crash.
Compared linear regression with k-nearest-neighbors regression on **20,640** California block groups using scikit-learn Pipelines, cutting test RMSE from about **$70,000** to about **$61,000**.
Ran an **A/B test** (permutation test, **5,000** simulations) to check whether drought years were truly drier than other years, rejecting chance at the 5% level (p = **0.026**).
Built **99%** bootstrap confidence intervals (**5,000** resamples) for monthly max temperatures, finding **9** of **12** months significantly hotter in 2019-2021 than in 1900-1960.
Flagged the multiple-testing risk of running **12** tests at once, and showed why unequal group sizes do not bias a permutation test.

Joined and grouped Gapminder country tables to track world population by decade (**2.6** billion in 1960 to **6.8** billion in 2020) and fertility versus child mortality across the **50** most populous countries.
Estimated that about **14.4%** of the world lived in extreme poverty around 2010 by joining each country's latest poverty rate with its population, then mapped poverty by region.
Built a k-nearest-neighbors classifier that labels **333** movies as comedy or thriller from script word frequencies, reaching **70%** test accuracy with **10** hand-picked features.
Analyzed the errors (darker comedies read as thrillers) and cut to **4** features, reaching about **78%** accuracy on a second test set.
Built a scalar autograd engine in plain Python that runs backpropagation by topologically sorting the computation graph and applying the chain rule at each node.
Trained an MLP built on the engine with gradient descent, cutting loss from **4.85** to **0.033** in **20** steps, and checked gradients against **PyTorch** autograd.
Tuned **PostgreSQL** queries on a baseball database by reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE plans: an index cut a MIN(salary) query cost from about **525** to **0.33**.
Measured trade-offs: the index made inserting **300,000** rows about **33%** slower, and clustering a table cut one query from **11.4** ms to **1.9** ms.
Modeled grid percolation with weighted union-find and virtual top and bottom sites, using a second union-find to prevent backwash.
Ran Monte Carlo trials to estimate the percolation threshold with its mean, standard deviation, and **95%** confidence interval.
Built a typing speed test that scores words per minute and accuracy, with autocorrect based on a recursive edit distance capped by a limit.
Wrote higher-order functions that simulate a dice game **1,000** times per setting to find the best number of dice to roll and compare strategy win rates.
Built a tower defense game with object-oriented programming: about **20** ant and bee classes sharing behavior through inheritance.
Ranked the top **20** LLMs from about **26K** human-preference battles by fitting a Bradley-Terry model (logistic regression) and comparing it to raw win rates on held-out battles.
Bootstrapped **200** resamples for confidence intervals on each model's rank, and grouped prompts into topics with LSA and K-Means to compare leaderboards by topic.
Built a style-controlled leaderboard that adjusts each model's strength for response length and formatting (bold, headers, lists).
Trained an MLP classifier on **70K** Fashion-MNIST images and made it robust to a rotated test set with rotation augmentation, a rotation-angle regressor, and test-time augmentation.
Built with **Claude**: a free website that helps California wildfire survivors write one clear letter to their insurer, in English, Spanish or Chinese.
Grounded a hosted **Llama** model on **Cloudflare Workers AI** in **15** numbered source notes; the server removes citations that do not exist, and nothing is stored server-side.
Built with **Claude**: a site that helps survivors write one clear insurance letter, grounded in **15** cited sources.
